_about: Curated short descriptions of major historical states, written for GeoHistory from general knowledge. "names" are the spellings the maps use; "from"/"to" limit the years in which the description is shown (they are display limits, not claims). Every year written in the text is checked by tools/build_curated.py against the Wikidata item of the entry's article; an entry is verified only when all of them match.

polities.text: The Roman state after the expulsion of its kings, traditionally from 509 BC, governed by annually elected magistrates and the Senate. It grew from a city-state in Latium into the ruler of the whole Mediterranean, and ended in civil wars from which Augustus emerged as sole ruler.

polities.text: The Roman state under emperors, from Augustus onward. At its height in the 2nd century it ruled from Britain to Egypt and Mesopotamia. It was divided for good into western and eastern halves in 395; the western half collapsed in the 5th century.

polities.text: The western half of the Roman Empire after the division of 395, ruled from Milan and then Ravenna. It lost its provinces to Goths, Vandals, Franks and others, and its last emperor was deposed in 476.

polities.text: The continuation of the Roman Empire in the east, with its capital at Constantinople, Greek in language and Orthodox Christian in religion. It recovered much of the west under Justinian, lost Syria and Egypt to the Arabs, and fell to the Ottomans in 1453.

polities.text: A loose empire of hundreds of principalities, bishoprics and free cities in central Europe, centred on Germany, whose emperor was chosen by prince-electors. It is usually dated from the coronation of Otto I in 962 and was dissolved in 1806 under pressure from Napoleon.
